_meta.purpose: Every number this project is allowed to print, with its provenance and its status. A poster, slide, abstract or viva answer may print a fact only if status is 'verified', 'computed' or 'published'. Anything else is a bug in the poster, not a rounding choice.
_meta.rule: If a number is not in this file, it does not exist. Add it here first, with a source, then print it.

statuses.verified: came back in a receipt produced by a run; source names the receipt
statuses.computed: derived deterministically by code in this repo; anyone can rerun it
statuses.published: quoted from an external paper; citation required; corpus tag is part of the fact
statuses.planned: a configuration, gate or target that has NOT been run. Never print as a result.
statuses.unverified: appears in older project documents with no locatable receipt. DO NOT PRINT until re-derived.
statuses.forbidden: a sentence that must never appear, with the reason

measured.label: C8 full synthesis, real dermoscopy
measured.source: runs/ph2-v1/C8.json, usable: true, clean tree, 5 epochs, width 16
measured.note: The learned half lifts localisation from 0.5384 to 0.8587 against its own classical control on the same split, and eliminates the three false claims. This is the C0-vs-C8 result the study is designed around.

measured.label: C0 vs C8 on one split

measured.label: C10 key memorisation test
measured.corpus: PH2, n = 120; trained on key K1, test images re-marked and read with K2
measured.note: THIS GATE FAILS (bound: drop <= 0.05). The network retains some key-specific structure rather than reading evidence in a fully key-agnostic way. Reported as a limitation, not smoothed over. It is not a collapse: 0.785 is still strong localisation on a key the model never saw.

measured.label: key dependence under a denied key
measured.corpus: PH2, n = 120; API images read with a key they were not marked with
measured.note: This is the security property WORKING, not a failure. Without the key the evidence is noise (measured E 0.010 -> 1.005) and the reader collapses. It is the measurement that answers 'isn't a learned reader just a learned forger'.

measured.label: dual-carrier fidelity on real dermoscopy
measured.source: run_matrix load_items, printed at load time
measured.note: Against the reference system's reported 40.47 dB. This is the one published figure the project matches on equal terms, because it needs no shared corpus.

measured.label: the full configuration matrix
measured.note: The first complete run of the matrix. C8 is the best of the twelve, and the ordering is informative rather than decorative: see M-23 and M-24.

measured.label: what the learned half is worth
measured.source: difference of M-16 and M-17, same clean-tree run
measured.note: The headline. Needs no external corpus.

measured.label: component attribution — the larger claim
measured.display: C1 (+AE alone) .7273 = +.1889 over C0. C8 (all eight) .8587 = +.3203 over C0. The other six components together add .1314.
measured.note: 59% of the total gain comes from adding the one-class AE alone. This is an ATTRIBUTION finding, and it is the kind of statement the field does not make because everyone reports one aggregate. It must be stated as measured on this corpus at this scale, not as a general law: 5 epochs and 72 training images is not convergence.

measured.label: single-component ablations
measured.display: C2 (+RefineNet only) .6929 · C3 (+AE+RefineNet) .7441 · C4 (+attention) .7489 · C5 (+degradation) .6345 · C6 (+segmentation) .7862 · C7 (+three-way) .6821
measured.note: C5 is BELOW C3 despite adding a component, and C7 is below C6. Neither is a bug: these are 5-epoch runs on 72 images, so configuration ordering at this scale is noisy and partly reflects optimisation luck. Report the ordering, do not over-read it.

measured.label: held-out family transfer
measured.display: C11 .7912 vs C8 .8587 — a drop of .0675; 1/3 false claims
measured.corpus: PH2, n=120, one tamper family withheld
measured.note: Transfers to an unseen family with a moderate drop, but produces one false claim where C8 produces none. Both facts reported.

computed.label: block-granular ceiling on pixel IoU
computed.corpus: synthetic disks of radius r on a 64x64 decision grid
computed.source: src/metrics.py block_ceiling(), reproduced by tests at r = 8/16/32/96/128/160
computed.headline: A flawless block classifier scores 0.809 at radius 32 and 0.854 at radius 48.
computed.note: THE central argument of the project. It is arithmetic, not a measurement, so it cannot be argued with. IMPORTANT: it bounds a DISK-shaped region at the worst-case block placement. A block-aligned region is not bounded by it and can exceed it -- the C8 per-area bucket at r~17px scored 0.849 against a disk ceiling of 0.618 because T1 copy-move is block-aligned. Report the ceiling as 'disk-model ceiling' and never as an absolute bound on all shapes.

computed.label: square-paste ceiling
computed.note: A block-aligned square paste is the one shape where a block system is not penalised. Any figure of the ceiling must include this line, or the ceiling looks like special pleading.
